keyFindings.description: Regression from acafc88f. Once the request ctx has ended, SetRoleWithPrevious starts neither the rollback of a claim that failed nor the old holder's topic cleanup after a claim that succeeded, because bus.Bounded returns at once under an ended ctx. The claimant's own UpsertWithin put can also land after the 503 with no claim behind it. Before, these ran under context.Background(), so a bus slower than the remaining budget but inside 10 s still cleaned up. A record then keeps notifications.role.<role> for a role its session does not hold, and heartbeat upserts only add topics (mergeForUpsert), so the topic stays until that session unsubscribes or ends. Roles are derived from topics: GET /v1/sessions and /v1/registry report it as a holder, Dispatch's route roster (internal/dispatch/api/issue_route_status.go) can name it the live holder (route_status live where it should be no_holder), and senderStamp puts the role in sender.roles, so recipients get a Reply Role hint (session/session.go:137-138). AGENTS.md:2038-2041 says this lasts 'until the next claim or unsubscribe', which is false for the old holder: a later claim cleans the holder it replaces, not this one. It also says only 'a claim whose write did not answer' skips the cleanup, but the old holder's cleanup is skipped after a claim that succeeded too.

storeAnswered (api.go:271-277) runs errors.Is over a joined error. SetRoleWithPrevious joins a lost compare-and-swap (nats.ErrKeyExists, an answer) with holderErr and rollbackErr. With ctx still live, when either is a call that did not answer (nats.ErrNoResponders, ErrConnectionClosed, a raw socket error), POST /v1/roles/set answers 500 'key exists ...' with no Retry-After and no busUnansweredPrefix, against the settled rule. Count the error as answered only when no joined part is unanswered.

The comment at :200-201 says the negative control is 'the same claim' asked before the freeze. The control at :215 is a hard claim of another role (role-store-control), and the same claim could not be its control, since the frozen write is described as the conditional create.

risksRecorded: /healthz now answers a JetStream-only stall '200 degraded' inside 3 s. Before, the 10 s wait timed out the Fargate container health check (curl -sf, timeout 5 s, 3 retries; infra/aws/rendering/listener.go:196), and ECS replaced the task. The self-health monitor does not restart on an unclassified JetStream timeout, so such a task is no longer replaced automatically. This follows from the architect's bound on /healthz together with the existing degraded-is-200 classification. It is recorded in the PR body's risk section for the architect, not held as a code defect.
